newsitem.title: USA: US stocks little changed at midday as rally pauses.
newsitem.headline: US stocks little changed at midday as rally pauses.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were little changed at Tuesday's midsession, as broad profit-taking robbed a strong morning rally of its steam.

The Dow Industrials gained two points to 6012 after surging to as high as 6044 in early activity. Declining issues outnumbered advancers on the NYSE by a roughly six to five margin on heavy volume of 234 million shares.
"You have to remember this all takes place after a big run on Friday and Monday," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer and Co.
Shares in CSX, also a Dow transport component, fell on news of the deal, dropping 3-1/8 to 46-3/8.

Analysts were unsurprised that stocks hit a snag today, noting yesterday's rally, which pushed the industrials to their first close over 6000 ever, represented a bit of a mixed blessing, because much of the strength came from oil stocks.
However, they also noted a more bullish sign, in that technology shares also seemed to find renewed spark.
"I think there's some carving back overall but it appears some money seems to be rotating to the techs," said Peggy Farley, chief executive at Amas Securities.
Wall Street had a heavy diet of earnings to digest early Tuesday, with a number of major banks and brokerages reporting.

Shares in the nation's largest banking company, Chase Manhattan Corp eased 1/8 to 82-3/8 after reporting third quarter earnings of $1.80 per diluted share versus $1.55 last year. The results were slightly below Wall Street estimates.
Citicorp shares gained 1-1/8 to 94-1/2 after the company reported third quarter earnings of $1.85 per fully diluted share, up from $1.62 a year ago.
Intel Corp surged three points to 110-1/2, a day after it reported much better than expected earnings. Several Wall Street firms raised earnings estimates on the company this morning.

In contrast, Bay Networks Inc fell 3-1/8 to 21-1/8, a day after it reported weaker than expected earnings and announced the resignation of its chief executive Andrew Ludwick. The shares were downgraded by a number of investment firms today.
Shortly after midday, renewed profit-taking pulled the Dow industrials to losses, sending the average down 28 points to 5982.
Among the shares selling off were those in oil companies Texaco Inc, Chevron Corp and Exxon Corp, the same companies that boosted the Dow higher on Monday.
